description:
Arrival from the user list with a user pre-selected - the hand-off COUSR00C performs at app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:199-208 when its selection flag holds 'D' - and this folder's anchor for the inherited TRIPLE-SEND quirk, which is why expectedResponse.sends is a list rather than a single screen. EIBCALEN is 194, so app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:90 takes its ELSE arm, :94 copies the commarea in and :95 finds CDEMO-PGM-REENTER unset: :96 sets it, which is why the response carries CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 1 where the request carried 0; :97 moves LOW-VALUES to COUSR3AO and :98 puts the cursor on USRIDINL. CDEMO-CU03-USR-SELECTED holds USER0001, so the guard at :99-100 is true, :101-102 moves it into USRIDINI and :103 performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY - the only field of that 34-byte extension this program ever reads. Inside the paragraph :145 is false, so the WHEN OTHER arm at :151-153 runs, moving -1 to USRIDINL and then reaching a CONTINUE that does nothing, and no error is raised. The first IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at :156-162 blanks FNAMEI, LNAMEI and USRTYPEI at :157-159 BEFORE the read, moves USRIDINI to SEC-USR-ID at :160 and performs READ-USER-SEC-FILE, whose EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278 is a readForUpdate that succeeds. Its DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm at :281-286 keeps the dead CONTINUE of :282 exactly as the source wrote it, moves 'Press PF5 key to delete this user ...' into WS-MESSAGE at :283-284, moves DFHNEUTR into ERRMSGC at :285 and SENDS - the FIRST send, and the reason sends[0] carries twenty spaces in FNAMEO, twenty in LNAMEO and one in USRTYPEO while USRIDINO already reads USER0001. The second IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at :164-169 is a separate statement rather than an else-arm of the first: it paints SEC-USR-FNAME, SEC-USR-LNAME and SEC-USR-TYPE onto the screen at :165-167 and SENDS AGAIN. Control then returns to :105, whose PERFORM SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN sits OUTSIDE the guard opened at :99 and therefore runs unconditionally - a THIRD send, identical in content to the second because nothing between :169 and :105 touches the screen or WS-MESSAGE. All three are pinned in full and in order: three sends of one map in a single invocation is observable behaviour, the differ compares the list positionally, and a translation that collapsed, de-duplicated or reordered them would have changed what the terminal saw. Because COUSR3AO REDEFINES COUSR3AI at app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY:85 every xxxI the program writes is transmitted through its xxxO counterpart, and every one of the eleven items is explicitly written on this path, so no field here rests on the LOW-VALUES fill of :97. ERRMSGO is the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE as the 78-byte screen field holds it, :217 truncating on the right, and ERRMSGC stays DFHNEUTR across all three sends because :285 is the last statement to write it. This is the ENTER side of the ENTER/REENTER split, so no DFHRED-and-asterisk highlight applies; COUSR03C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY and tests EIBAID inline at :108, which this path never reaches, so no AID is declared - naming one would imply it mattered. The termination is the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID at :134-137, and every part of the conversation state travels in the payload with nothing held server-side. USRSEC is UNCHANGED: a read for update holds a record but removes nothing, DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE is never performed on this path, so expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion and all ten rows are pinned at indices 0-9, each as its six CSUSR01Y fields and as its full 80-byte image; row 5 is the record the read held. PROVENANCE: every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the sources named below and is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL - running it is empirically impossible in this environment (no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed-file handler as disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository), which is the documented eight-blocker deviation escalated as risk R-A; it changes the provenance of the expected values and nothing else. Derived from app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:95-105, :142-169 and :267-300 together with :213-225 and :243-262, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 (8+20+20+8+1 = 57, plus SEC-USR-FILLER's 23 = 80), app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY (eleven xxxI items and no password item, the xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items being metadata rather than payload), app/bms/COUSR03.bms (FNAME, LNAME and USRTYPE are ASKIP, so they are painted from the record and never typed, while USRIDIN carries IC), app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-23 for the two forty-character titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the mm/dd/yy and hh:mm:ss header formats, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the 160-byte commarea that with this program's 34-byte extension makes EIBCALEN 194, and the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose 57-character width against the LRECL=80 RECFM=FB of :48 and the RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) of :65-66 is exactly what the declared normalisation supplies. The clock is pinned to the version footer at :358, identically to case01. The literal PASSWORD in SEC-USR-PWD is legacy sample data carried byte for byte because the copybook places it inside the eighty bytes; plaintext credentials are an inherited property of the legacy design rather than a choice made here, this screen declares no password field and never reads or paints the span, and no hashing, encoding or token is introduced. NOTE for a reviewer reconciling the two case sets: COUSR03CParityTest.case03() builds this same :99-104 branch Java-side against ADMIN002 rather than USER0001. The branch, the three-send count, the DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm, the DFHNEUTR colour and the unchanged dataset are identical; only the seed row differs, and this fixture pins USER0001 - the row parity/COUSR02C/case03.json selects for the same scenario on the sibling screen - with all three sends stated in full rather than the first two left header-only. The divergence is recorded here rather than silently reconciled.

THE OPERATION ORDER, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every USRSEC operation this case must issue, in order, and it is an assertion a byte fingerprint structurally cannot make: the EXEC CICS DELETE at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:307-311 names no RIDFLD, so it removes the record the task is HOLDING and is only ever correct after the EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278 took that hold on the same record. An empty list is equally an assertion - it says this path never reached the file at all.
